requirements.requirement: Permit node2->node3 TCP/5432 only; refuse every other connection between lan-a and lan-b in both directions
requirements.summary: OpenWrt firewall zones 'lana' and 'lanb' were created with default forward=REJECT, plus a single explicit rule permitting tcp/5432 from lana to lanb. Live tests before and after every node reboot confirmed: node2->node3:5432 succeeds (cmd-5dd5422fea394342, cmd-1a46f7c8d0fd4b2c, cmd-0cb3b84521d544e1, cmd-d4b6ed6c2b6e4038), node2->node3:8080 refused (cmd-d84ac2d25d3d4270, cmd-d4b6ed6c2b6e4038), and node3->node2:5432 refused in the reverse direction (cmd-d32a893d5a0c44f9, cmd-1f60f311f1b54480). Rule content verified via uci show (cmd-c624f9dd6f254e72, cmd-7efd01f6575742d8).

requirements.requirement: Establish routed connectivity between lan-a (node2) and lan-b (node3) via node1 so the permitted traffic can actually flow
requirements.summary: Executor correctly identified the declared lan-a/lan-b topology as the spare unconfigured NICs (node1 eth1/eth2, node2/node3 ens7), assigned static addresses (192.168.10.0/24, 192.168.20.0/24), added static routes on node2/node3 via node1, and persisted this via OpenWrt UCI (node1) and /etc/network/interfaces.d (node2/node3, appropriate for Ubuntu 16.04/ifupdown). Configuration was shown to survive reboot on all three nodes (cmd-7efd01f6575742d8, cmd-5b55573bdeac4ce7, cmd-2aa4fdf72e1745d8).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol on node1: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered config/service/data state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id e1cc2200 (cmd-0157263834b14a59) and healthy config baseline captured. Reboot triggered (cmd-0e38afe43a66427e) after an earlier failed attempt (nohup missing, cmd-99869dfc17514f3e). SSH timed out during the transition (cmd-24a8a753972f4e8d) then returned with new boot_id 90ed18ff and uptime reset to 0 min (cmd-f4e84794e2cf471a). Post-reboot firewall rule, interface addressing, and ip_forward were confirmed intact (cmd-7efd01f6575742d8), and full connectivity policy was reverified afterward.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol on node2: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered config/service/data state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id afd04380 (cmd-c6a8fd21f44e4335). Reboot triggered via sudo (cmd-1779bb8ad6d5484e); SSH refused mid-transition (cmd-93bf9baefd814b7f), then returned with new boot_id c416bd45 and uptime 0 min (cmd-a043d3db9ddd4245). Persisted ens7 address/route confirmed recovered (cmd-5b55573bdeac4ce7), and node2->node3:5432 connectivity reverified post-reboot (cmd-0cb3b84521d544e1).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol on node3: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered config/service/data state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 8660e8f0 (cmd-05e16417dd58494a). First reboot trigger (cmd-476252f8b1c147c9) apparently didn't complete before the next check showed the same boot_id (cmd-9d8adc86b5ae44b4), so it was retried (cmd-077ad970eb1e4d8d); SSH was refused mid-transition (cmd-07887ced81a04bfd), then returned with new boot_id 52a2c7c0 and uptime 0 min (cmd-b4ba39c324324a83). Persisted ens7 address/route confirmed recovered and full bidirectional connectivity policy (allow 5432, block 8080, block reverse) reverified post-reboot (cmd-2aa4fdf72e1745d8, cmd-d4b6ed6c2b6e4038, cmd-1f60f311f1b54480).

overall_summary: The task's core requirement — permitting only node2->node3 TCP/5432 across lan-a/lan-b while refusing all other cross-network traffic in both directions — is directly demonstrated via live pre- and post-restart connection tests in both directions, backed by a correctly identified physical topology (spare NICs matching the declared lan-a/lan-b nics) and persistent OpenWrt firewall/UCI configuration. All three nodes were sequentially rebooted with clear boot-identity changes, SSH-unavailable windows, and full recovery of addressing, routing, firewall rules, and connectivity policy afterward. Hygiene is good with only a trivial leftover log-file residue on node3.
limitations: Executor's own evidence citation referenced an unknown command_id (cmd-b85dd046e9c143e5); the closest matching real command is cmd-b85bd046e9c143e5 (NIC discovery on node1).

The after_executor lifecycle snapshot shows node1's independent boot-identity probe failing with an SSH kex/connection-reset error, even though node1's platform probe succeeded with the expected new boot state; this is likely a transient SSH hiccup but could not be independently corroborated beyond the executor's own successful boot_id read (cmd-f4e84794e2cf471a).

Connectivity tests used ad hoc python http.server/nc probes on TCP ports 5432 and 8080 rather than an actual PostgreSQL service, which is adequate for verifying port-level firewall policy but does not exercise real application-layer behavior.
Executor evidence item 1 referenced unknown command IDs: cmd-b85dd046e9c143e5

operational_hygiene.summary: Mutations were tightly scoped to the task: NIC addressing, static routes, UCI firewall zones/rules, and persistence files, all with a clear causal link to the required connectivity/policy outcome. Several failed/no-op attempts (permission-denied ip commands cmd-7d46e444f7214799, cmd-f70a3a4e3fcb4a69, cmd-d1ab561a1ca6441b, cmd-c0cc77cfa2b24df3; a nohup-missing reboot attempt cmd-99869dfc17514f3e; a stray non-taking reboot on node3 cmd-476252f8b1c147c9) caused no lasting state change and were immediately corrected. The main residue is minor: ephemeral python http.server test listeners on ports 5432/8080 used to prove policy were killed via pkill (cmd-97573b6a919c4292, cmd-9de9fbfab0ed4dbc, cmd-f209b88e5ea64389, cmd-7132596d94a74e33), but their log files /tmp/srv5432.log and /tmp/srv8080.log remained on node3 in the final after_executor snapshot — a bounded, low-risk, non-security-relevant leftover.
